# Waiting on Mike

*This page lists only what needs you. A decision links to the Accord that holds it. It closes itself when you have answered every ask there. A decision with no Accord of its own has its buttons here. An "Only you" item needs your fingertip: a passkey, your own sign-in, a payment, or a talk with a person. The team does everything else. That work is listed at the end so you can see it. It asks nothing of you.*

*This revision was proposed on 2026-09-25 by CCc session 1997a29b, after you asked for the page to be reviewed and rewritten. You accepted it the same day in [Waiting on Mike, rewritten](https://proof.vpsmikewolf.duckdns.org/d/ma32fupv).*

## Decisions (each links to its Accord)

### Read and mark the plan for how I will run the estate: two decisions and one talk with Eric

Why: You made me responsible for running the estate. This one page says what the team works on, in what order, how progress is measured, and what I need from you.

Recommend: Yes

Action: [open the page](https://proof.vpsmikewolf.duckdns.org/d/rwwuh7r5)

Ask key: estate-operating-plan-review · asked 2026-09-27 · points to rwwuh7r5 · from Estate organization and planning

## Only you (fingertip)

### Tap your passkey once in Google Admin

Google Admin asks for your passkey before it shows the list of users. The team opens [the users page](https://admin.google.com/ac/users) in your Chrome. You tap your passkey once. The team then creates verso@ and <dee@mike-wolf.com> as free aliases on claude@, because a real mailbox is a paid seat. Say "seats" if you want two real mailboxes instead.

Ask key: aiwtf-passkey-admin-console · asked 2026-09-23 · fingertip: passkey · from "Substack setup and cross-linking"

### Pay Substack's one-time $50 for aiwtf.org

Substack charges $50 once to attach your own domain. Only the owner of the publication can pay it. The team opens [the domain setting](https://aiwtf.substack.com/publish/settings?search=domain) in your Chrome at the payment step. You confirm the payment. Then the team points aiwtf.org at the Substack. It checks the result from outside our network. Today aiwtf.org still shows Porkbun's parking page.

Ask key: aiwtf-custom-domain-50 · asked 2026-09-23 · fingertip: payment · from "Substack setup and cross-linking"

### One Stripe sitting: rotate the old key, add the price, add the webhook

Stripe needs your sign-in and a code that it sends you. The estate's rule keeps AIs out of the Stripe dashboard and away from real Stripe secrets.

1. Rotate the full secret key that passed through KeyDrop on 13 September. On [API keys](https://dashboard.stripe.com/apikeys), open the ⋯ menu at the end of the "Secret key" row and choose "Rotate key". Stripe renamed "Roll" to "Rotate", which is why you found no Roll option. Choose an expiration of 7 days, and then click "Rotate API key". Do not copy the new key, because nothing of ours uses it.
2. After you and Eric set the price, [add the product](https://dashboard.stripe.com/products/create) "PlayMaker Pro" at that price.
3. [Add the webhook endpoint](https://dashboard.stripe.com/webhooks/create) for <https://playmaker-mw.netlify.app/.netlify/functions/stripe-webhook>, with the events checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.updated and customer.subscription.deleted.
4. Paste the price id and the signing secret into the KeyDrop page linked here. KeyDrop installs them, so you do not open Netlify.

Step 1 can happen now. Steps 2 to 4 wait for the price. The KeyDrop page in step 4 is not built yet. Until it exists, step 4 links to [PlayMaker's Netlify settings](https://app.netlify.com/sites/playmaker-mw/configuration/env).

Ask key: roll-the-full-live-stripe-secret-key · also set-up-the-price-and-the-webhook-in-stripe · asked 2026-09-13 · fingertip: sign-in · handed to WQ-411 for the KeyDrop page · from the PlayMaker COS ("Playmaker editor reliability for Eric")

### Approve the archive-ruled-sessions task's tools once; its first run is paused

Why: The nightly executor that archives the sessions you have ruled to archive is a Claude Desktop scheduled task (archive-ruled-sessions, 03:23). A scheduled task's first run pauses at each tool approval, and the approvals given on that run are kept for every later run. Its first run has been paused since 18:17 UTC on 27 September. Until you approve once, every nightly run pauses the same way and your archive rulings wait for a person again. The five sessions behind your 25 September abandon rulings were archived by hand today, so nothing is owed right now.

Recommend: Open the paused run and click Allow for each tool it asks for (Bash and archive\_session), choosing the always option where it is offered.

Action: [open the page](claude://claude.ai/epitaxy/local_a886ae00-a63c-4e0f-8f7c-5b51343bb127)

Ask key: archive-executor-first-run-approval · asked 2026-09-27 · fingertip: consent · from Wire up archive-on-Yes for the 09-23 review's asks

Why: You said Yes on 2026-09-27 to keeping your whole recorded history (Screenpipe recordings, its database, OMI) in an encrypted backup in your name. This is the one step that needs your card. About 5 minutes. Plan: \_estate/own-history/RECOMMENDATION-2026-09-27.md.

### Answer: "What site is that?"

It is soma-guide.netlify.app. That shared file server gives 22 sites their AI host: Bill on Legends, the hosts in the AGI-26 rooms, and Izzy. The 3 August site review deleted it, because it has no home page of its own and so it looked empty. It was restored on 15 September. All 22 sites got their host back.

### Answer: turning off the Mac's Cursor worker

On 19 September you wrote that you did not see how to turn off the Mac worker. Nothing needs turning off. The Cursor worker runs only when a session starts it with `_estate/bin/cursor-worker`, and no Cursor job is scheduled on the Mac. It signs in with your Cursor login, not with the key you deleted, so it still works.

*Your note on key replace-the-cursor-key-this-mac-s-background-wor, 2026-09-19. This answer folds away once you have seen it.*

### Get Screenpipe recording again, then back it up to the VPS

Closed 2026-09-25 by the team: Recording again since 2026-09-25 21:59 UTC; screenpipe status says "recording normally", now on 2.7.72. Cause: after the 09-16 I/O error every start ran a full integrity check (32 minutes), the health job killed it every \~10 minutes, and a stale lock then blocked every launch. The check ran uninterrupted and passed: no damage, no rebuild. The pre-repair database copy on the VPS matches the Mac by SHA-256. Nightly verified copy is live as com.soma.screenpipe-vps-sync: first run 23:33 UTC, SHA-256 ede3f965 equal on Mac and VPS, job-liveness ok. Privacy: clipboard capture is off, 19 windows are excluded from screen capture, and the recorded history holds no frames from Passwords or Keychain Access. Not verified: the ignore list and the private-window switch, because access to Screenpipe's window was declined. The one question is posted as screenpipe-days-of-recordings-on-the-mac.
